summary: Clallam County lookout on Blyn Mountain: 1934 pole tower, 1960 40-ft timber tower; removed 1969 per Weebly; cab and top moved to Beausite Lake.

facts.design: First lookout: 90-foot pole tower with 8x8-foot cab and ground-house quarters (1934). Replacement: 40-foot timber tower with 14x14-foot live-in cab (1960).
facts.status_note: Tower removed (1969 per Weebly). Cab and top 10 feet moved to Beausite Lake in the 1970s. Willhite's undated caption says all footings are still in place.

access.note: Willhite: drive-up on good gravel roads with no gates; no closure found in these pages

visit.trail_note: Willhite: snow or fallen trees are the only likely obstacles

events.note: First lookout: 90-foot pole tower with 8x8-foot cab and ground-house quarters; Weebly dates the start of work to 1933
October windstorm picked up the ground cabin and hurled it against a tower leg
Aircraft Warning Service station activated August 12, 1942; Willhite says the use ran through 1944
Willhite: Olga Hughett staffed Blyn from 1950; newspaper counts (ninth year in 1960, 14 years by 1966) do not match
Newspaper item quoted on Weebly: Blyn lookout manned by Olga Hughett
40-foot timber tower with 14x14-foot live-in cab replaced the first tower; a 1966 newspaper gives 45 feet
Willhite's end date for Hughett; 1966 newspaper items show other lookouts
Ann Forest spent the summer as lookout; Karen Ronning took over after Forest left for school (October 1966 item)
Weebly lists the tower as removed in 1969
Cab and top 10 feet moved to Beausite Lake; sources say 'in the 1970s', and the year shown is the first year of that decade
Registered November 26, 2011; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register, firelookout.com and Willhite give 1934; Weebly dates the start of construction to 1933. The story uses 1934 and mentions the 1933 start.
Register and Willhite give 40 feet, as does Weebly's 1960 entry. A 1966 newspaper says 45 feet. The story uses 40 feet and reports the newspaper figure.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 12.2 is the 1960 40-ft tower; the first (1934) tower was 90 ft, and the story says so. Unresolved: when Hughett started (Willhite says 1950; newspaper counts point to a later start), and whether the tower or cab was on county or private land (Willhite says the tower was county-owned and later that the cab went to private property). The 1960 newspaper spells the name Hughes; the story uses Willhite's spelling. The 1969 removal date rests on Weebly alone. Brief record matched on 1934 build and 2011 registration. No photo URLs captured because fetch_text returns text only.
